newsitem.title: USA: Clinton set to fill four Cabinet posts.
newsitem.headline: Clinton set to fill four Cabinet posts.

text.p: President Bill Clinton was expected to nominate four new Cabinet secretaries on Friday, as well as the head of his Council of Economic Advisers (CEA), administration officials said.

The officials, who asked not to be identified, said the president appeared to have settled on his choices to run the departments of Labour, Energy, Transportation and Housing and Urban Development (HUD).

Clinton on Thursday offered the chairmanship of the CEA, a three-member council which performs economic analysis for the president, to Federal Reserve Board Governor Janet Yellen, said one administration official.

Administration officials said Clinton was likely to name Rodney Slater, the head of the Federal Highway Administration, as secretary of transportation and Andrew Cuomo, an assistant secretary of HUD, as HUD secretary.
Slater is a long-time Arkansas colleague of the president and was a Clinton confidant and travelling companion during the 1992 presidential campaign. He would replace Federico Pena, who is resigning.
Cuomo, the son of former New York Gov. Mario Cuomo and married to a daughter of the late Sen. Robert Kennedy, is one of the best-connected young Democratic officials in the nation.
As an assistant secretary at HUD, where he served under Secretary Henry Cisneros, who is retiring, Cuomo has been deeply involved in programmes to fight homelessness.
Officials said Elizabeth Moler, the head of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, was Clinton's likely choice to run the Energy Department, replacing Hazel O'Leary.
The choice to find a replacement for Labour Secretary Robert Reich was the most difficult, officials said, with Clinton leaning toward various candidates at different times.
They said Clinton seemed to have settled on Alexis Herman, an influential White House aide with close connections to civil rights groups, to be labour secretary.
"The most contentious, long-drawn-out selection was for labour," said one official who asked not to be identified.
Earlier officials had said Clinton was believed leaning toward Representative Esteban Torres, a California Democrat, for the Labour post, and they had discounted Herman's prospects.
Another official cited for the position was former Sen. Harris Wofford, a Democrat who visited the White House earlier this month to be sounded out for an administration job.

Clinton was expected to announce the appointments, as well decisions to re-appoint current secretaries for Interior, Agriculture, Education and Veterans Affairs, at a midday news conference on Friday.
But they cautioned it was possible that he might change his mind on the appointments.
They also said that several lower level jobs were likely to be filled, with Bruce Reed, a White House aide, moving up to be Clinton's chief domestic policy adviser.

Thomas "Mack" McClarty, Clinton's former White House chief of staff, was likely to be given an expanded role and title. After stepping down as chief of staff, McClarty remained at the White House as a counsellor who maintained contacts with business and specialised in Latin American commerce.
Clinton himself on Thursday declined to tip his hand on the appointments. "We're working very hard on it," he told reporters without committing himself to any announcements.
